insight.title: Fungi Redesign Their Networks in Real Time to Save Energy
insight.subtitle: Without a brain, underground mycelium dynamically transitions from a wide-reaching search grid into a single, high-speed transport pipeline.
insight.notificationHook: Fungi redesign their networks in real-time

sections.text: To find food, underground fungi cast a wide, delicate net in all directions. But the instant a single thread touches nutrients, this sprawling search grid vanishes, replaced by one thick, high-speed transit cord.

The fungus systematically dissolves its empty search branches. It quickly reclaims those raw materials and channels them directly into reinforcing the single, winning route, cutting down on unnecessary maintenance costs.

This fluid architecture allows the network to constantly self-optimize. By transitioning from an expansive search engine to a dedicated cargo highway, it never wastes energy maintaining infrastructure it does not need.
Fungi build perfect infrastructure by constantly dismantling the unused.
